ingredients.item: Firm white fish fillets or steaks (cod or halibut)

instructions: Start the rice first. Rinse 1 1/2 cups basmati rice and cook it the way you usually do.
Rinse the 3 pieces of kudampuli and soak them in 1/4 cup hot water. Peel and finely chop the shallots, and mince the ginger and garlic separately. Chop the tomato.
Cut the fish into 2-inch pieces, pat them dry and sprinkle with 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Heat the coconut oil in a wide, deep skillet over medium heat. Add the curry leaves and stand back, they spatter.
Add the shallots and the ginger and cook for 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until the shallots are soft and light golden.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato and cook for 3 minutes, until it breaks down.
Add the chili powder, coriander, turmeric and 1 tsp salt. Stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the kudampuli with its soaking water, 1 cup of the coconut milk and 3/4 cup water. Bring it to a boil, then cover and cook for 4 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium-low and slide in the fish in a single layer. Swirl the pan to coat it. Don't stir, the fish breaks.
Cover and cook for 8 minutes. Pour in the rest of the coconut milk, about 2/3 cup, and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.

You're cooking the fish to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one piece there. No thermometer? Break a piece open. It's done when it flakes easily and is opaque all the way through.
Take the pan off the heat and lift out the kudampuli pieces. Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the rice. Slice the green chilies and set them on the table for anyone who wants heat.
method_notes: Swasthi's Recipes leads (5 from 7 ratings, so this is a fallback). Table and Traditions, Take It Easy Chef and Yummy Tummy Aarthi all build the sauce on kudampuli, Kashmiri chili, coriander and coconut oil; they differ on coconut milk (Swasthi and Table and Traditions use it, the others leave it out). Slit green chilies moved to the table, and fenugreek and the second tempering were left out. The curry is better the next day; reheat gently.
